directed_tree_reconstruction.description: Directed binary-tree hierarchy reconstruction (Figure 5 / Appendix D.1.1), depth 7 (255 nodes), 2D embedding. The paper reports this result qualitatively: symmetric embeddings neither reveal the hierarchy direction nor preserve the distances, while Finsler MDS reveals the direction and highly preserves all distances. scores.json scores the exact paper tree; scores_train.json / scores_test.json score visible / hidden trees of the same topology with per-level edge weights drawn around the paper's (0.5, 1.5, 0.1) and shuffled node labels. A method that returns an invalid output or misses a claim threshold on any instance is scored as failed (every metric set to the value of the empty prediction).

normalized_stress.description: Global directed-distance reconstruction error: sqrt(sum (d_pred - D)^2 / sum D^2) over all ordered node pairs, with d_pred computed by the evaluator from the submitted 2D coordinates and drift. Mean over the experiment's instances.

distortion.description: The paper's Table 1 distortion: mean over ordered node pairs of (d_pred - D)^2 / D (stress with weights 1/D), which emphasises the short distances that carry local structure. Mean over instances.

map_at_10.description: Diagnostic only. Tie-aware mean average precision of the 10 nearest directed neighbours. Every target distance is tied within a tree level, so this is 1.0 for any embedding that keeps levels apart, including a degenerate one that collapses each level to a point; it cannot rank methods on this benchmark.

asymmetry_rmse.description: Constraint: RMSE of the antisymmetric part, (d_ij - d_ji) - (D_ij - D_ji), over ordered pairs. Must stay <= 0.10 on every instance (eligibility gate); its small continuous weight rewards direction accuracy beyond the gate.

asymmetry_correlation.description: Diagnostic only. Correlation between predicted and target antisymmetric components.

symmetric_rmse.description: RMSE of the symmetric part, (d_ij + d_ji)/2 - (D_ij + D_ji)/2, the component a direction-only fit cannot reduce.

hierarchy_alignment.description: Diagnostic and gate. Signed concordance, over pairs of nodes on different tree levels, between the hierarchy and each node's uphill potential (total incoming minus total outgoing predicted distance); 1 = every shallower node sits uphill, 0 for symmetric distances. Must be >= 0.80 on every instance.

distance_preservation_pass.description: Figure 5 claim check, graded: clip(1 - normalized_stress / 0.10, 0, 1) averaged over instances; 0 when the method is not eligible.

asymmetry_preservation_pass.description: Figure 5 claim check: fraction of instances with asymmetry_rmse <= 0.10 (1 for every eligible method, 0 when not eligible).

hierarchy_direction_pass.description: Figure 5 claim check: fraction of instances with hierarchy_alignment >= 0.80 (1 for every eligible method, 0 when not eligible).

directed_tree_depth5_reconstruction.description: The same directed hierarchy reconstruction on depth-5 trees (63 nodes), matching Figure 5's various-depth trees. Qualitative expectations, instance families and the eligibility rule are the same as for the depth-7 experiment.

cora_digraph_reconstruction.description: Paper Table 1 (Cora, embedding dimension 10): reconstruct the directed shortest-path distances of the Cora citation digraph (LINQS; largest weakly connected component: 2485 papers, 5209 citations) from a 10-dimensional embedding per node and one drift vector. A citation graph is nearly acyclic, so the gym follows the paper's own directed-tree construction to make every directed distance finite: following a citation costs 1, travelling against it costs 3 (the tree's 1.5 / 0.5). scores.json scores the whole component; scores_train.json / scores_test.json score induced breadth-first subgraphs of 400 papers with shuffled labels (5 visible / 10 hidden). Of the paper's Table 1 dimensions {2, 5, 10, 50}, 10 is the smallest at which the reference (Finsler SMACOF) beats the Euclidean embedding on both distortion and MAP on the visible slice; in 2D it does not (see PROGRESS.md). The paper embeds with a neural representation learner; the gym scores whatever embedding a method returns, and the reference is Finsler SMACOF. The eligibility rule is shared with the tree experiments. 'results' holds the paper's Table 1 Finsler values at dimension 10 (neural embedding of the whole graph, the paper's own distance handling; not on this gym's scale) and the claim they support (euclidean_gain_pass: Finsler 1, Euclidean 0). The gym scores its Euclidean baseline as not eligible (a symmetric embedding cannot pass the asymmetry gate), so its score rows hold the failure values; its raw distortion and MAP are in details*.json, and the paper's Euclidean values are listed under _paper_table1_10d_reconstruction.

distortion.description: The paper's Table 1 distortion: mean over ordered node pairs of (d_pred - D)^2 / D (stress with weights 1/D). Mean over instances.

map.description: The paper's Table 1 MAP (graph reconstruction): for every paper that cites another paper of the instance, rank all other papers by predicted directed distance from it and take the average precision of the papers it cites; mean over citing papers, then over instances. Exact ties are broken pessimistically.

normalized_stress.description: Global directed-distance reconstruction error, sqrt(sum (d_pred - D)^2 / sum D^2) over ordered pairs (the uniform-weight stress the paper's MDS objective uses). Must stay <= 0.25 on every instance.

asymmetry_error.description: Constraint: RMSE of the antisymmetric part, (d_ij - d_ji) - (D_ij - D_ji), divided by the RMS of (D_ij - D_ji); 1.0 for any symmetric (Euclidean) embedding. Must stay <= 0.80 on every instance (eligibility gate).

symmetric_error.description: Diagnostic only. RMSE of the symmetric part, (d_ij + d_ji)/2 - (D_ij + D_ji)/2, divided by the RMS of (D_ij + D_ji)/2.

euclidean_gain_pass.description: Table 1 claim check: fraction of instances on which the method has both lower distortion and higher MAP than the Euclidean embedding of the same instance (the evaluator's frozen Euclidean SMACOF baseline); 0 when the method is not eligible.

_setup_note: The paper reports the tree experiment only qualitatively (Figure 5); its 'results' encode those qualitative claims as pass checks (1 = claim holds, 0 = it does not) and are unchanged. The citation experiments reproduce Table 1's claim (Finsler embeddings of real digraphs have lower distortion and higher MAP than Euclidean ones) on the paper's Cora and Citeseer digraphs in embedding dimension 10; their 'results' encode that claim as euclidean_gain_pass (Finsler 1, Euclidean 0). The gym's directed distances (reverse traversal at cost 3), 400-node subgraphs for train/test and SMACOF reference differ from the paper's neural setup, so the paper's Table 1 numbers (listed under each citation experiment's 'results' for dimension 10, and below for dimension 2) are not on this gym's scale; they are context, not targets.

_paper_table1_2d_reconstruction.note: Paper Table 1, embedding dimension 2: distortion (lower is better) and MAP (higher is better), Euclidean vs Finsler, whole graphs, neural representation learning. Not on this gym's scale (see _setup_note).

_paper_table1_10d_reconstruction.note: Paper Table 1, embedding dimension 10 (the gym's citation setting): distortion and MAP, Euclidean vs Finsler, whole graphs, neural representation learning. Not on this gym's scale (see _setup_note).
